2026-08-12T12:34:10.6432310Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6432854Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6433304Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6434033Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6434553Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6435303Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6437791Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6440815Z >
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6444623Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6448807Z >
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6450023Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6451248Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6451469Z ### How to Use
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6451776Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6453328Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6454618Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6454867Z ```bash
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6455644Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6456726Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6457610Z ```
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6457865Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6458438Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6459201Z ```bash
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6459934Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6461114Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6462363Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6463457Z ```
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6463717Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6464647Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6465984Z ```bash
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6466753Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6467769Z ```
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6468202Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6468625Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6469627Z ```bash
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6470345Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6471626Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6472649Z ```
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6561665Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6562099Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6562783Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6565170Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6568076Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6568291Z ```bash
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6568883Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6570205Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6571439Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6571881Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6572624Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6574192Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6575419Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6576051Z ```
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6576307Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6577499Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6579179Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6579395Z ```bash
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6580343Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6581675Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6583351Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6584074Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6584699Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6585949Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6586732Z ```
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6586989Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6587284Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6588748Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6590259Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6591739Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6593272Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6595014Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6595843Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6596063Z ### Notes
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6596345Z 
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6597306Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6599745Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6601727Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6603658Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6605521Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6607183Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6609472Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-12T12:34:10.6610556Z </mcp-clis>
